content:
Logan Wright: heads up, need eyes on a telemetry schema change for perf-canary + per-model baselines. goal is to add stable model+version tags (and runtime build/kernel tags) without breaking existing dashboards/alerts. can folks review proposed attribute names + backcompat plan?

Logan Wright: context: canary alert payloads want `model`, `model_version` (canonical), `runtime_build`, `kernel_id`, `hardware_sku`, `region`, and we need these in both metrics + traces (so we can link from alert -> trace). today we have a bunch of semi-stable labels like `model=llama3_70b_instruct` that sometimes drift based on catalog aliasing.

Caleb Johnson: yep. what’s the proposed schema exactly? are we talking OTLP attrs + prom labels derived from them?

Logan Wright: yup. OTLP attributes as source of truth; prom uses a constrained mapping.

Logan Wright: draft (namespaced):
- `rw.model.canonical_id` (string, stable UUID-ish from model registry)
- `rw.model.name` (string, human readable, current alias)
- `rw.model.version` (string, registry version like `2026-02-12` or semver-ish)
- `rw.runtime.build_id` (string)
- `rw.runtime.kernel_set_id` (string) (maps to kernel selection build/tag)
- `rw.hw.sku` (string)
- `rw.region` (string)

Logan Wright: for prom mapping we’d keep the existing `model` label for now but introduce `model_canonical_id` + `model_version` on canary-specific series only (or behind allowlist) to avoid cardinality blowups.

Nadia Rahman: +1 on canonical id. question: do we need both `rw.model.name` and `rw.model.canonical_id` in baselines? baselines should key on canonical id + version + hw sku + runtime build right?

Logan Wright: yeah baseline key we’re leaning: canonical_id + version + hw sku + runtime_build (+ optional region). human name purely for display.

Omar El-Sayed: from runtime side, we can emit these, but we need the model registry to hand us canonical id + version at request time. right now we have `model_handle` and `model_route` which can be alias-y.

Quentin Harris: model registry can provide that. we already added a canonical identifier export in PR 18577 (model-registry) but it’s not being threaded through everywhere.

Quentin Harris: one nuance: “version” is different for open models vs finetunes. open models have registry version (pin) and may also have upstream “base” version. i’d keep it simple: `rw.model.version` == registry pin/version string. if we want upstream later, add `rw.model.upstream` attrs.

Caleb Johnson: re backcompat: biggest risk is existing queries/dashboards expecting `model` label only. if we add new labels to existing high-volume series, ingestion cost jumps + cardinality. we should avoid turning on new dimensions globally.

Allison Grant: +1. also we have alert policies that assume `model` and maybe `tier/region` only. if labels change shape, we’ll page ourselves.

Logan Wright: agreed. plan is additive:
1) keep emitting current labels/attrs unchanged (`model`, `model_route`, etc)
2) add *new* OTLP attrs (rw.model.*) to spans + selected metrics
3) for prom, map new attrs only on perf-canary metrics (low volume) and maybe runtime “summary” series that are already sampled.
4) later: deprecate `model_route` usage in dashboards; migrate to canonical id behind the scenes.

Caleb Johnson: can you be explicit on “selected metrics”? which meter names?

Logan Wright: for perf canary: everything under `perf_canary_*` (service-owned) gets full label set.

Logan Wright: for runtime: only these (already aggregated / low-card) get extra tags:
- `rw_runtime_request_latency_ms_bucket` (BUT only with `model_canonical_id` if we keep it limited to top-N models, otherwise too many time series)
- `rw_runtime_tokens_per_sec` (same constraint)
- scheduler queue time hist (same)

Nadia Rahman: top-N constraint is important. baselines for long tail models can still key on `model` name for now? or are we saying baseline store only for curated set?

Logan Wright: baseline store is only for covered models (top + high-risk list). so emitting canonical id for those only is ok.

Omar El-Sayed: implementation question: where do we apply allowlist? runtime side or telemetry pipeline side?

Caleb Johnson: pipeline side preferred (collector/transform) so we don’t need to redeploy runtime for config churn. but runtime still needs to *emit* the attrs so pipeline can choose to pass through / drop.

Omar El-Sayed: ok. runtime can add attrs on spans and on the internal metrics event before aggregation, but prom exporter might strip unknown attrs unless mapped.

Caleb Johnson: right. for OTLP metrics we can keep attrs; for prom we map labels explicitly. we can also do transform: if attr exists but not allowlisted, drop it to avoid “accidental fanout”.

Allison Grant: how are we preventing accidental fanout if someone adds `rw.model.version` to a high-QPS metric? that’s a footgun.

Logan Wright: propose a “label guardrail” in the metrics aggregation helper (PR 19209-ish) + collector config policy:
- collector drops any `rw.model.*` attrs unless metric name matches `perf_canary_*` OR metric has `rw.safe_dims=true` attr set by runtime
- and even then, enforce allowlist for model ids (top models) when exporting to prom

Caleb Johnson: make sure the guardrail is visible in code review. ideally tests that fail if `rw.model.version` shows up on non-canary metrics.

Nadia Rahman: what about traces? traces are less cardinality sensitive but still huge volume. do we keep `rw.model.canonical_id` on all inference spans?

Caleb Johnson: traces can handle high-card better, but storage cost is real. i’d still keep it; it’s important for joining alerts -> traces. maybe sample traces more aggressively for long tail models.

Allison Grant: from incident response POV, having the canonical id on the trace is gold. otherwise you click from alert and you can’t filter correctly.

Quentin Harris: another backcompat thing: if we ever rename `model` label from alias -> canonical, a lot breaks. please don’t overload existing `model` field.

Logan Wright: 100%. `model` stays human-readable alias for now. canonical gets its own field.

Omar El-Sayed: also note we have internal “shadow” models / compatibility variants (quant profiles). should that be a separate dim? otherwise version comparisons can be misleading.

Nadia Rahman: yeah, we’ve seen that in baseline week1. same “model” but different quantization profile → different TPS. we need an explicit dim for that in baseline key.

Logan Wright: good catch. proposal:
- `rw.model.variant` (string) for serving variant / quant profile / context length config. examples: `fp16`, `int8_kv`, `longctx_128k`.

Caleb Johnson: ok but this is another cardinality dimension. can we keep `rw.model.variant` only on canary + traces, not on general runtime metrics?

Logan Wright: yes, canary + traces only initially.

Allison Grant: is `rw.model.variant` stable naming? we need consistent values.

Quentin Harris: model registry can provide a canonical “serving profile id” for the deployment. might be better than free-text variant. e.g. `rw.serving.profile_id`.

Omar El-Sayed: we already have internal “profile” object when we build the engine. we can plumb `profile_id`.

Logan Wright: cool, let’s do that:
- `rw.serving.profile_id` (string)
- optional `rw.serving.profile_name` (string) if we want display.

Caleb Johnson: versioning/backcompat on schema: do we need a formal schema version field? like `rw.telemetry.schema_version=2`?

Logan Wright: i’d prefer not for now. since this is additive, consumers can feature-detect attrs. adding a schema version becomes another thing to keep consistent.

Nadia Rahman: but for baseline store ingestion, it’s helpful to know if a record includes canonical id vs not.

Caleb Johnson: you can just check presence of `rw.model.canonical_id`. no need schema version.

Allison Grant: rollout plan? do we dual-write and then flip dashboards?

Logan Wright: rollout proposal:
- week 1: runtime emits attrs on spans; canary emits full dims; collector drops by default except canary
- week 2: enable pass-through for inference spans (traces) globally; add trace search facets
- week 3: enable prom label mapping for canary metrics (already low volume) + update dashboards
- week 4+: consider adding canonical id to a small set of runtime metrics for top models only (behind allowlist)

Omar El-Sayed: sounds good. i’ll open runtime PR to add `rw.model.canonical_id`, `rw.model.version`, `rw.runtime.build_id`, `rw.serving.profile_id` on inference spans and the canary-path metrics events.

Quentin Harris: i’ll sync with you on the registry API fields. for version string: we should ensure it’s immutable and doesn’t change with alias updates.

Caleb Johnson: please also include a mapping doc for old fields -> new fields so dashboard owners can migrate. even a short table in confluence.

Allison Grant: + runbook note: “if canonical id missing, check runtime build < X or collector config not rolled out”. helps oncall.

Logan Wright: will do. action items:
- [Logan] post collector transform + label guardrail design + add tests
- [Omar] runtime emission PR
- [Quentin] confirm registry field names + stability
- [Allison] review alert/dashboard impact + make sure we don’t change existing `model` usage yet

Nadia Rahman: can you also confirm how this affects baseline artifacts in object storage? we should store canonical id + version + profile_id as the primary key.

Logan Wright: yep. we’ll update baseline artifact schema to include those fields; keep legacy `model` string as display field.

Caleb Johnson: last thing: please don’t use dots in prom label keys (prom doesn’t like it). OTLP attrs can be `rw.model.canonical_id` but prom labels should be `model_canonical_id` etc.

Logan Wright: yep, OTLP uses dotted; prom exporter maps:
- `rw.model.canonical_id` -> `model_canonical_id`
- `rw.model.version` -> `model_version`
- `rw.runtime.build_id` -> `runtime_build_id`
- `rw.runtime.kernel_set_id` -> `kernel_set_id`
- `rw.serving.profile_id` -> `serving_profile_id`

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: as long as the existing dashboards don’t suddenly get new label sets.

Logan Wright: acknowledged. no label changes on existing runtime series without explicit signoff + allowlist.

Omar El-Sayed: ok grabbing this. will @ here when PR is up.

Quentin Harris: same, i’ll drop a note once registry side is ready.

Caleb Johnson: thanks. once there’s a PR, tag me and i’ll review collector config + retention impact.
